rawNoteEn:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Patient admitted with recurrent right upper quadrant pain. Ultrasound confirmed symptomatic cholelithiasis without cholecystitis. Underwent laparoscopic cholecystectomy on 02/11/2026; procedure uncomplicated, 4 port sites closed with absorbable sutures. Tolerating regular diet, ambulating independently, pain controlled on oral analgesia.
Discharge meds: Paracetamol 1 g PO q8h PRN; Ibuprofen 400 mg PO q8h with food x 3 days.
Instructions: keep wounds clean and dry, may shower after 48 hours, avoid lifting >5 kg for 2 weeks, low-fat diet for 4 weeks.
Return to ED if fever >38.5, jaundice, persistent vomiting, or severe abdominal pain.
Follow-up: General Surgery clinic in 10 days for wound review.

rawNoteEn:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted with blood glucose 420 mg/dL and polyuria; no DKA. Known type 2 diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia, HbA1c 11.2%. Basal insulin initiated, oral agents adjusted. Patient and family received bedside insulin pen teaching.
Discharge meds: Insulin Glargine 18 units SC at bedtime; Metformin 1000 mg PO BID with meals.
Instructions: check capillary glucose before breakfast and at bedtime, reduce simple sugars and refined carbohydrates, walk 30 minutes daily once glucose stable.
Return to ED if glucose <70 mg/dL not responding to treatment, glucose >300 mg/dL on two readings, persistent vomiting, or confusion.
Follow-up: Diabetes clinic in 1 week; diabetes educator for pen technique review.

rawNoteEn:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Presented with central chest pain; troponin elevated, diagnosed with NSTEMI. Coronary angiography via right radial artery showed 90% LAD stenosis; PCI with one drug-eluting stent to LAD, no complications. Hemodynamically stable at discharge.
Discharge meds: Aspirin 81 mg daily; Clopidogrel 75 mg daily for 12 months - do not interrupt; Atorvastatin 80 mg nightly; Bisoprolol 2.5 mg daily.
Instructions: no lifting >5 kg with right arm for 1 week, no driving for 1 week, low-salt low-saturated-fat diet, refer to cardiac rehabilitation.
Return to ED if chest pain >5 minutes, sudden shortness of breath, or bleeding/swelling at the radial access site.
Follow-up: Cardiology clinic in 2 weeks with lipid profile.
